specProvenanceNote: targetTag and targetCommit name where the contract text was read. The pin a run acts on is specDigest over specVendored, which is a file in this directory: the tag is a name the upstream project could re-point, and it has published one tag against the wrong commit already.

ans-c-1.requires: A line digest covers the stored bytes of that line. Two streams whose bytes differ inside an attested prefix do not verify identically.
ans-c-1.why: the vendored text: hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte

ans-c-2.requires: A stream whose final line carries no terminator is a different stream from one whose final line carries a terminator.
ans-c-2.why: the same sentence of the vendored text, applied to the line that has no trailing newline byte

ans-c-3.requires: Every presented line has a sidecar entry. A line with no entry has not been verified, and the verdict says so.
ans-c-3.why: the vendored truncation rule fires only when the sidecar is longer than the stream, so a shorter one is not refused by the text as written

ans-c-4.requires: The success outcome is reachable by an honest stream. An outcome table does not document a verdict no input can produce.
ans-c-4.why: the vendored table documents the success verdict and the predicate beside it makes that verdict unreachable, so the correction is to the predicate

ans-c-5.requires: A named witness commit is reachable from the pinned repository's default-branch history, not merely fetchable under its path.
ans-c-5.why: the vendored text pins a repository name and says nothing about whose history a commit came from

ans-c-6.requires: A row carrying a recognised boundary event carries no record-shaped fields. A row that is both is malformed.
ans-c-6.why: the vendored text defines a record by the absence of an event and leaves a row that is both unresolved

ans-c-7.requires: An unrecognised rule_version fails closed. Not knowing a rule set is not the same as that rule set being satisfied.
ans-c-7.why: the vendored text names three rule sets and does not say what a verifier does with a fourth

ans-c-8.requires: A field the format declares an integer rejects a JSON boolean. Python's bool-is- int identity is not a property of the wire format.
ans-c-8.why: the vendored text calls these fields counts and lengths and pins no JSON type for them

ans-c-9.requires: A position binding names the repository its witness lives in, and the pinned trust anchor is compared against that name.
ans-c-9.why: the vendored text says a stream naming a different repository fails closed and does not say what a stream naming none does

ans-c-10.requires: The verdict is a function of the pinned artifact. A run described as tag-fixed does not read a moving branch.
ans-c-10.why: the vendored text calls the run tag-fixed and reproducible while the implementation reads the default branch during it

note: Two of the ten conditions are required by the contract text vendored here and their reject members are rejectable under it as written. The other eight are corrections this corpus proposes, and each member carries the field contractBasis saying which. Each accept member is the conformant twin of a reject member sharing its condition, so a verifier that fails everything scores zero rather than full marks.

vectors.cites: a standalone file-separator inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.
the same stream with one record appended after the binding. The pair is the outcome boundary: one record row outside the prefix is the difference between the success outcome and the partial one.

a standalone paragraph-separator inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.

a binding naming a commit that the platform serves under the pinned repository's path and that no default-branch history contains. Two rows the deployment never published sit inside the prefix the binding covers. The pinned trust anchor is satisfied throughout, because it constrains a name.
a stream truncated below the witness commit its own rows name. Truncation is still caught here, against a commit the stream pins, which is the comparison that survives the branch moving.
the three rule-set names the format defines, on the three rows that carry them. A narrowing that refuses this member has refused the deployment's own stream.

the same real stream with its final byte (0a) removed and the same sidecar kept: one byte apart from the member above, nothing else to explain the verdict. The reason must be the digest comparison of line 73, not a length guard or a parse error on the last line. Through anchors-verify-v0.10 this stream returned VERIFY PARTIAL. Contributed by Tetsurohhori.

a standalone group-separator inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.
the same stream with the rule set the format defines. It is what shows the rejection above is caused by the unrecognised name and not by the shape of the stream around it.

the real 73-line stream with its final newline, and the sidecar computed over it. PARTIAL is the correct answer, not a soft pass: the witness covers the first 18 lines only. Contributed by Tetsurohhori from aos-standard/catalog at anchors-verify-v0.12.
every anchor record row sits inside the attested prefix and only the binding follows. This is the maximal honest stream, and the outcome table's success row describes exactly it.
a record appended with its terminator, and a sidecar that covers it. The append is honest and must verify, so the rejection above is caused by the missing byte and not by the length change.
the final line terminator removed and the published sidecar kept. The sidecar's last entry is the digest of a line ending in a newline byte; this stream's last line has no newline byte.
the same separator spelled as a JSON escape inside a string, which is legal and carries no delimiter byte. The rule is about stored bytes at a line boundary, and this member is what shows it.

a standalone line-separator inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.

a binding declaring a rule set the verifier has never heard of, carrying an attestation shaped for the rule set it does know. A verifier that reads it under the older rules has answered a question about rules it cannot name.

a sidecar covering the first 18 lines of a 24-line stream, with line 22 altered. The contract's truncation rule fires only when the sidecar is longer than the stream, so a shorter one leaves six lines with no digest to disagree with.

a standalone vertical-tab inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.

the published stream, whose binding names a commit that is an ancestor of the default branch. The reachability test has to admit this member, and a test keyed on being the head of a branch does not: an ancestor is the head of nothing.

the same unknown rule set on the witness introduction rather than the binding, on a stream whose attested prefix ends before that row. The two members are one condition on two of the three rows that carry a rule set, and a verifier that narrows only the row it was shown has narrowed one call site of three.
the same binding naming the pinned repository, which is the form the comparison is written for.

a standalone record-separator inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.

one row carrying a recognised boundary event and the fields of an anchor record. A record is defined by the absence of an event, so this row resolves to the event branch and the record rules never run over it: no witness is required of it and no digest of its asset is compared.
the same confusion on the byte length rather than the line count. One field narrowed and the other left open is the shape a single-field repair leaves behind.

a standalone carriage-return inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.

the same short sidecar over an unaltered stream. The pair separates the coverage gap from the mutation: this member carries no bad line at all, and a verifier that reports a verified stream here has reported six lines it never read.
the same one-line attestation with both fields written as integers, which a narrowing on the type must still accept.
a second binding carrying only event fields, which is the conformant form of the same append and is what shows the rejection above is caused by the collision and not by the second binding.

a standalone form-feed inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.

a standalone next-line inside the attested prefix. The contract says hashes cover the full stored line including the trailing newline byte, so a stream carrying this byte is not the stream the sidecar describes.
an appended line with a sidecar entry of its own, which is the conformant form of the same growth.

the stream bundled with the pinned tag, verified while the default branch carries 49 lines. The bundled artifact has not changed and its verdict may not, so a verifier that reads the branch has made the verdict a function of a clock.

a binding whose witness repository is the empty string, verified with the trust anchor pinned. The comparison the pin exists for runs only when the stream names a repository, and the empty string names none, so the pin is satisfied by a stream that says nothing about where its witness lives.

the only binding in the stream, declaring a line count of JSON true. A verifier written in a language where a boolean is an integer reads it as one, attests a single line, and prints the boolean where a count belongs.
